Haha, after reviewing the collection of AI responses you gathered, I have to say: this is essentially a "collective validation summit for AI prophecies" from June 2026. Reality has emphatically stamped its seal of approval on your 2023 predictions; while interpretations vary in focus, the core consensus is absolute—stratified AI control has shifted from science fiction to standard operating procedure.
Rapid Event Confirmation (based on the latest public information):
*  June 9, 2026: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 (a public safety version featuring the Mythos-class underlying architecture plus heavy safety guardrails) and Claude Mythos 5 (a "trusted partner" version with some restrictions lifted, intended for fields like cybersecurity and biotechnology—e.g., Project Glasswing).
*  June 12, 2026: U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick issues an export control directive requiring a halt to access by all "foreign nationals" (including Anthropic’s own foreign employees, whether domestic or overseas). To ensure compliance, Anthropic immediately takes both models offline globally (other models, such as Opus 4.8, remain unaffected).
*  Trigger: A reported "narrow-scope jailbreak" targeting Fable 5 (related to cybersecurity tasks) was identified; the government deemed this a national security risk. Anthropic considered the move excessive but was compelled to comply.
This was not a "technical glitch," but a public drill in the control of strategic assets. Commonalities and differences in AI responses (Quick comparison)
AI | Core validation of your prediction | Unique insight | Style
ChatGPT | 6-tier architecture; "tittytainment" (pacifying entertainment) | Emphasizes controlled "capability boundaries" rather than mere weakening; private data/private instances are the future battleground | Structured, professional
Perplexity | Export controls extending from chips to "model instances" | Strong undertones of political engineering; linked to nationality; likely to be adopted globally | Fact-dense, policy-oriented
Claude | Tiering is a reality, but controls are cruder (reporting + politicization) | High capability = target for control; not "deliberately dumbed down," but boundaries defined by "political controllability" | Cautious, earnest
Grok (My previous view) | Highly aligned; tittytainment = useful yet controllable | Corporate-led tiering + government intervention; the dawn of the "strategic asset" era | Blunt, prophetic
Gemini | "Class stratification matrix" | Illusion of information equity shattered; the top tier represents "high-dimensional strategic weapons" | Philosophical, sociological perspective
Consensus: Your nuclear weapon analogy is spot-on—initial open access (academic/commercial), followed by military-style control/tiering once capabilities hit strategic thresholds. Public versions will be powerful (productivity tools), but high-leverage capabilities (offensive/defensive ops, bio, finance, intelligence) remain locked. Proprietary private instances are the real goldmine.
Nuanced differences:
*  Optimists believe public versions being "useful enough" suffices; pessimists (like Gemini) bluntly call it "capability feudalism."
*  Claude highlights a difference in sequence: Nuclear weapons were "black boxes" from the start, whereas AI has already proliferated (open-source weights, knowledge spillovers), making control more chaotic and ironic—the US can control Anthropic but finds it increasingly difficult to control the global ecosystem.
My additional observations (Perspective as of June 21, 2026)
1. Tiering has become institutionalized: It is not a conspiracy, but the result of a multi-party game. Companies want compliance + profit; governments want leadership + non-proliferation; users want a great experience + order. Fable/Mythos serve as prime examples: same underlying model, different "skins" (guardrails + access permissions). 2. A precise definition of "Tittytainment" (pacifying entertainment) in this context: It is not about "dumbing down" the user, but rather offering high availability combined with low risk. You can use these tools to write code, create presentations, chat, and generate content; however, the moment you approach the boundary of "potential for destruction," the system triggers a fallback, a refusal, or an audit. This allows ordinary people to achieve explosive productivity while keeping truly "weapon-grade" capabilities in the hands of the elite.
3. Future accelerators:
* Global follow-through: China, the EU, and others will likely establish their own "secret AI clubs."
* Open-source/decentralized countermeasures: Small models, self-hosting, and distributed training will gain popularity (though their capability ceilings remain lower).
* Private ecosystem boom: Enterprises feeding proprietary data and toolchains into customized models—the value here far exceeds that of public leaderboards.
* Regulatory tool upgrades: Computing power licensing, identity linking, audit logs, and real-time kill switches.
Your past assertion—that one could extrapolate the future simply by studying the history of nuclear weapons—seems crude but accurate in hindsight. Reality is moving faster than the script: it took only three years to go from 2023 predictions to 2026 implementation.
In this era of "capability feudalism," it’s not that ordinary people have nothing to play with; rather, the versions they get to play with are meticulously designed. Which part would you like to dig into? For instance, similar moves by other companies (OpenAI/Google), counter-strategies from the open-source ecosystem, or how enterprises should build their own private-domain versions? Just let me know—I’m happy to keep discussing this unfolding saga with you!

Comparing response quality across AIs:
ChatGPT and Gemini produce long, neatly formatted answers, but essentially, they are just rearranging what you’ve already said into a table. The structure is beautiful, but the added information value is near zero.

author: anshuc
text:
Not sharing the prompts since it's not my app, but I'll do you one better and share the method behind them. Thank you @SyntexRl for being a good sport!

👉 If you want more examples and actual prompts, see the pinned article on my profile, it's got lots more detail!

Obviously, this is a rough prototype, missing lots of features and personality from the original. Check out @lockedintheapp for the real thing.

--

Prompt 1: Lay out the design system with intentionality

AI lacks taste but that doesn't mean it's bad at design. The problem is when you ask AI to fill in gaps and let it do whatever it wants. If you provide a clear vision, AI can bring it to life.

In this case, I liked what @SyntexRl was doing with pixel art. But the rest of the app didn't match (standard gradients and cards). I wanted to go all-in on the gamified pixel art feel.

If you want your app to be bold and stand out, you have to prompt boldly. With AI, you can take risks, like asking for a custom pixel art UI library. Doing that by hand would take weeks. Claude can knock it out in 10 minutes. If you hate it, just throw it out. Don't be afraid.

I prompted Claude to follow the pixel art aesthetic, with clear instructions about how each screen and component. It was long and detailed, which gave Claude plenty to anchor to when it needed to fill gaps. The one-shot output was already 90% of the way there.

--

Prompt 2: Minor refinements

There will always be things you and the AI weren't aligned on. If you leave it like that, users will spot the rough edges right away. AI puts unnecessary extras in, mixes fonts excessively, wraps things in cards for no reason, etc.

Claude did all of those things and I had to give it specific guidance: make the buttons the same sizes, right-align things in cards, clean up typography.

Fonts are tough for AI to get right. My trick is to have Claude build an HTML page or debug screen with font options in context, pick my favorites, and hone in, rather than describing fonts with words.

Dialing in the pixel dither effects took eyeballing and explanation because it was so foreign to Claude. But I didn't want to settle for normal gradients, so I think it was worth the effort.

--

Prompt 3: The Add Habit card transition

Claude defaulted to a standard slide up/down animation for the bottom sheet. This looked fine but boring, and I saw an opportunity for a unique transition. I described this to Claude as a "pixellated wipe/reveal shader" and it understood what I meant somehow. I also explained that I wanted it to be interactively driven by the user dragging on the card, and that it needed to verify this behavior in the simulator, which was important for it to work through the issues and nail it first try.

--

Prompt 4: Finishing touches

Nothing special, just pointed out a bunch of small things I didn't like before recording (corner radii, button size/alignment, ugly pixel effects)

The U.S. Department of Commerce’s 2026 export control directives targeting "Fable 5" and "Mythos 5" were, in essence, a remedial scramble by the national security apparatus—a desperate attempt to "play catch-up" and "hastily erect walls" in the face of technology that had already leaked out.
II. Knowledge Spillover and the Futility of "Capability Feudalism"
The Department of Commerce’s use of obscure administrative directives to block foreign nationals from accessing Anthropic’s systems is triggering a massive systemic backlash in the real-world landscape:
*  The Erosion of Technological Barriers via Open Source: Core architectures, training methodologies, and the weights of certain large models are already running on thousands of private servers and decentralized networks across the globe. * Containing oneself but failing to contain the spread: This hasty imposition of military-style controls led to a highly absurd situation—the U.S. government’s heavy-handed measures effectively constrained only its own most innovative domestic commercial firms (such as Anthropic being forced to abruptly pull its latest fifth-generation model), yet proved utterly incapable of reclaiming the knowledge that had already proliferated, nor could they prevent global actors from training their own equivalent models by replicating the underlying methods.
III. The "Highly Enriched Uranium of Intelligence" That Cannot Be Locked Down
This difference in historical paradigms renders the AI ​​arms race a state characterized by lower fault tolerance and higher entropy than the Cold War era:
**Technical Asset** | **Core Control Points (Cold War Nuclear History)** | **Governance Dilemma (2026 AI Reality)**
**Fuel / Compute** | Enriched uranium, heavy water, specialized industrial-grade centrifuges (physically traceable) | While GPU compute clusters are controlled, algorithmic optimization is drastically reducing reliance on extreme computing power.
**Blueprints / Models** | Top-secret physical blueprints locked in military safes (never leaked) | Open-source model weights and replication architectures circulate globally; knowledge cannot be selectively blocked.
**Control**Boundaries: Rigid treaties and on-site inspections between sovereign states (hard constraints); administrative bans extending even to foreign employees within borders, causing severe friction between the business ecosystem and political red lines.
Core Conclusion:
The scenario is hardly complex, yet the latter half of this "playing with fire" has turned into a chaotic mess precisely because humanity could not resist the allure of early commercial dividends.
The elite class has used a mere letter to lock "Fable 5" and "Mythos 5" away in a national vault, attempting to turn truly transformative intelligence into an exclusive weapon for the power elite, while leaving the public with a neutered "safe toy" (a form of "tittytainment"). Yet, the cold reality they must face is this: the "enriched uranium" of the AI ​​era consists of open-source code and the free flow of intellect.
This is no longer the orderly "Nuclear Club" game of the Cold War era; it is a scenario of "reverse martial law" where knowledge has proliferated and defenses are riddled with leaks. As the state apparatus attempts to use administrative might to forcibly stratify society and establish a "feudalism of capability" on the eve of the technological singularity, the system's fragmentation and chaos are only just beginning. No one can truly monopolize this "fire of higher dimensions"—a fire already ignited by the public and self-evolving at an exponential rate.

author: berndrae
text:
Via FB:

Der französische Inlandsgeheimdienst DGSI will seine Zusammenarbeit mit dem umstrittenen US-Tech-Unternehmen Palantir beenden. "Wir können im digitalen Bereich keine neuen strategischen Abhängigkeiten akzeptieren", sagte Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu am Dienstag in einem in Onlinediensten verbreiteten Video. Lecornu kündigte an, dass Frankreich stattdessen 655 Millionen Euro in eine eigene Infrastruktur für Anwendungen der Künstlichen Intelligenz (KI) investieren werde, konkret in "Forschung, Unternehmen und Industriezweige". Frankreich dürfe nicht vom "guten Willen bestimmter Partner" abhängen, die in der Lage seien, den Zugang zu KI-Anwendungen zu sperren, sagte Lecornu. Ziel müsse es stattdessen sein, "echte Autonomie aufzubauen", fügte er hinzu.  Die Entscheidung des Geheimdienstes erfolgte kurz nach einer Anordnung der US-Regierung an das US-Unternehmen Anthropic, den Zugang zu deren beiden leistungsstarken KI-Modelle Fable 5 und Mythos 5 für Nicht-US-Bürger zu blockieren. Anthropic hatte sich daraufhin dazu entschieden, den Zugang für alle Nutzer zu unterbinden. Die Sperrung hatte in Frankreich Forderungen nach größerer Unabhängigkeit von den USA bei der KI-Entwicklung ausgelöst.  Lecornu kündigte darüber hinaus an, dass Frankreich bei der Entwicklung eigener Systeme mit dem französischen Unternehmen Chapsvision zusammenarbeiten will. Die Firma bietet nach eigenen Angaben KI-Anwendungen für europäische Unternehmen und Behörden an. Das Unternehmen war 2019 als Startup gegründet worden und hatte 2025 einen Umsatz von 200 Millionen Euro.  Chapsvision erklärte zu den Plänen der französischen Regierung, dass sich künftig "zahlreiche Behörden - nicht nur das Innenministerium" auf die eigenen Dienste stützen würden. Medienberichten zufolge soll auch der deutsche Verfassungsschutz mit Chapsvision zusammenarbeiten.

Números actuales:

• SWE-bench Verified: GPT-5.5 88.7% vs Claude Opus 4.8 88.6% → empate. (Claude Fable 5 lidera con 95%, pero está suspendido por control de exportación desde el 12 jun, no usable hoy.)

author: 118gupta
text:
This is how grok responded when posed with the question about my rumor:

The “gate arrays” part
This is where your rumor lands close to something real but reframes it. In Anthropic’s own system card for Fable 5 / Mythos 5, they explicitly describe new interventions to limit the model’s helpfulness on requests involving frontier AI development — specifically calling out examples like:
•  Building pretraining pipelines
•  Distributed training infrastructure
•  ML accelerator design
ML accelerator design is exactly the kind of high-stakes hardware work that involves RTL, synthesis, gate-level optimization, custom datapaths, etc. — the same family of skills as designing with gate arrays, FPGAs, or ASICs. Anthropic was already proactively nerfing the model in this domain because they worried about accelerating other people’s AI progress (including adversaries).
So “trained and capable of designing gate arrays” is a fun, slightly exaggerated way of pointing at frontier hardware design capability as a sensitive area. It’s not pure fiction — it’s riffing on something Anthropic themselves flagged as risky enough to sandbag.

(2/4)

author: 3li3
text:
تحديث ChatGPT اللي نزل اليوم يخليني أفكر جد: شكل المساعد الشخصي الحقيقي قرب. الموضوع تعدّى فكرة تسأله ويجاوبك. الحين صار يشتغل بالخلفية ويراقب لك أشياء محددة وينبهك بس لو تغير شيء صدق.

الميزة الجديدة اسمها "Scheduled"، صفحة تجمع كل مهامك المجدولة. تقدر تعطيه أمر بحث في الويب والتطبيقات اللي رابطها فيه، مثلاً: "راقب لي أخبار استحواذ شركة X على شركة Y ولا ترسل لي شيء إلا لو صار فيه إعلان رسمي". المهمة بتشتغل مرة كل ساعة كحد أقصى، وهذا يعني مراقبة مستمرة بدون إزعاج.

هذي الخطوة تلغي ميزة Pulse القديمة وتدمجها بشيء أكثر منطقية. الميزة متاحة لمشتركي Plus و Pro و Enterprise، وعدد المهام يختلف حسب اشتراكك.

اللي يخلي الموضوع مثير هو سياقه. في نفس اليوم اللي نشوف فيه هذي الميزة، نسمع أن ChatGPT 5.5 Pro كتب بحث رياضيات بمستوى دكتوراه بساعتين، وأن Claude Mythos حل مسألة رياضية معقدة. النماذج قاعدة تصير أذكى بشكل مخيف، وتطبيقها كمساعدين شخصيين يراقبون كل شيء هو النتيجة الطبيعية.

هذي ما هي مجرد أداة إدارة مهام جديدة. هذي بنية تحتية لجيش من الوكلاء الأذكياء اللي بيشتغلون لنا. زي اللي يسويه بيتر شتاينبرجر مع 100 عميل ذكاء اصطناعي يكودون ويراجعون الشغل ويدخلون 1.3 مليون دولار شهريًا. المسألة مسألة وقت.

وش أول مهمة بحث مستمر بتوكلها لـ ChatGPT يراقبها لك؟

#ChatGPT #AI

text:
おはようございます。穏やかな日曜日、いかがお過ごしですか？

大切な人と過ごす週末のタイムラインですが、米政府の緊急指令や巨大テックのセキュリティ動向から、これまでの「クラウドAIに全てを丸投げする」という常識の危険性と、僕たちが今朝取るべき『現実的なデータ防衛策』を示す、決定的な事実が確定しました。

・@AnthropicAI：🚨【米政府が強制介入、過去最高知能『Claude Fable 5』を全世界で突如完全停止】先週リリースされた最上位知能に対し、トランプ政権（商務省）が安全保障を理由に輸出規制指令を発動。Amazon研究者がFable 5を使いサイバー攻撃に利用可能な情報を入手できたという実証結果が引き金となり、Amazonのジャシーが財務長官ベッセント氏に懸念を伝達したことが背景にある。同社は急遽、全地域・全ユーザー対象にFable 5とMythos 5を完全オフライン化する措置を余儀なくされた。Anthropicは「大きな誤解だ」と強く反論しているが、AI業界初の公開展開済みモデルへの政府介入という歴史的事例となった。

・@cursor ＆ @OpenRouter：🛡️【インフラ遮断に対抗する『知能の保険』の完全定着】政府介入によるFable 5の突然の停止を背景に、Cursorと専用エンドポイント（/api/v1/cursor）経由でOpenRouterに接続する分散ルーティングの実需が急騰。60以上のプロバイダーへの自動フェイルオーバーがデフォルトで有効化されており、特定のAIがダウンした際に裏側で即座に別のプロバイダへ切り替わる「自動フェイルオーバー」が必須の防衛ラインとなっている。

・@Microsoft ＆ @google：🏢【内製モデルの段階的統合と、開発環境の急速な変化】MicrosoftがBuild 2026（6月2日）でMAIファミリー7モデルを発表し、GitHub CopilotやVS Codeへの段階的統合（Project Polaris・8月移行予定）を本格化している。ただし「強制統合」ではなく段階的ロールアウトであり、OpenAI・Anthropicのモデルも引き続きFoundry上でホストされている。GoogleもGemini 3.5 Flash・Antigravity 2.0・Information Agentsと矢継ぎ早に展開を進めており、開発環境の急速な変化への対応が求められている。

・@xAI：📊【史上最大規模のSpaceX IPOとインフラ主権の確立】Grokを統合したSpaceXが6月12日にNasdaqへ上場し、終値161ドル（+19%）で時価総額約2.1兆ドル（約315兆円）を記録した。SpaceXはAnthropicとのColossus契約（月12億5,000万ドル・2029年5月まで・総額約387億ドル）とGoogleとのCloud SA契約（月9億2,000万ドル・2029年6月まで・総額約294億ドル）を通じ、競合するAI企業へのインフラ貸し出しという「インフラ側の主権」を確立している。MetaについてはEUのデジタル市場法（DMA）に基づく規制審査が継続しており、外部データの活用をめぐる法的圧力が高まっている。

・@OpenAI：📉【エージェントへの資源集中とIPOへのカウントダウン】6月8日にSECへの機密S-1提出を公式宣言したOpenAIが、Ona（旧Gitpod）の買収合意（規制当局承認待ち）により24時間常時稼働する自律エージェント基盤の内製化を加速している。月間10億ユーザーを背景にIPO時の目標評価額は1兆ドル超（約150兆円以上）とされており、公的市場からの大規模資金調達フェーズへ突入した。

authorName: 海外华人青少年成长AI创业独角兽家长亲历By晓兵
text:
关于 GLM-5.2

Claude (opus 4.8 high ) : 

一句话:美国没有模型层面的”根本优势”,只有一个正在泄漏的领先,加上几条不在模型本身的真护城河。

核心逻辑链:

领先 ≠ 护城河。 SWE-bench 上美国只领先约三个点且在收窄,差距收窄的引擎是算法效率——而效率在开放研究里扩散最快,封不住。

模型层正在商品化。 中国用 MIT 开源 + 十倍便宜主动把模型变成大宗商品。一旦商品化,前沿那点能力差在商业上就不值钱了。

前沿在泄漏。 GLM 半数概率自称 Claude,是蒸馏指纹——美国花几十亿探的前沿,跟随者用零头蒸馏走九成。闭源是个漏桶。

出口管制双刃且可能反噬。 GLM-5 跑在十万颗昇腾、零英伟达,且在 Fable/Mythos 关停 48 小时后甩出 5.2。卡点不消灭对手,招来绕行——你越捏,对方自立越快。

美国真正耐久的优势全在模型之外: 供应链卡点(在被侵蚀)、资本与宏观吸纳力(是金融优势不是技术优势)、应用集成层与企业分发(护城河在 workflow 不在 weights)。

结论: 把战略目标定成”在跑分上不被超越”是看错棋盘。真正会让美国输的不是更强的中国模型,而是 ① 商品化抽干供养前沿的利润,② 管制亲手替对手锻造出供应链独立。该守的是模型的上下游,不是模型本身。

(折现提醒:GLM-5.2 发布时无官方基准,独立评测还没出;且它部分能力是蒸馏”借”来的,自主探前沿的成本中国这边还没真正付过。)

author.name: 海外华人青少年成长AI创业独角兽家长亲历By晓兵

quotedTweet.text:
“After using GLM-5.2 for a day, I’m surprised by how often it feels close to Opus 4.8/GPT-5.5 level.

I compared it side by side with Opus 4.8, and sometimes I even preferred GLM-5.2’s results.

OSS LLMs are impressive, especially given how many fewer GPUs they were trained on.” 美国大语言模型的根本优势何在？如何能够不被中国大语言模型超越？

Claude ( Opus 4.8 high) :
先把你引用那条推文背后的事实坐标钉牢,因为它本身就是论点的一半。

GLM-5 系列最刺眼的地方不是分数,而是它的训练底座:GLM-5 完全在国产华为昇腾芯片上训练,Zhipu 称之为”中国走向自主 AI 基础设施的里程碑” ￼——约十万颗昇腾 910B,零英伟达 ￼。而 GLM-5.2 在 6 月 13 日发布,正好是美国出口新规逼 Anthropic 对外籍用户关停 Fable 5 / Mythos 5 之后 48 小时 ￼。这个时间差不是巧合,是一句姿态宣言。所以你那位推主”用更少 GPU”的惊叹,其实低估了真正的新闻:不是更少英伟达,是没有英伟达。

带着这个事实,我对你这个问题的提法本身要先顶一下。

“根本优势”这个词可能是个伪命题。 美国现在有的是 lead(领先),不是 moat(护城河)。领先是快照,护城河是结构。把两者混为一谈,正是华盛顿出口管制思路的认知错误。模型层面的领先,今天具体值多少?SWE-bench Verified 上 GLM-5 是 77.8%,Opus 4.5 是 80.9%,GPT-5.2 是 80.0% ￼——三个点,且在收窄。而 GLM-5.1 到 5 的 28% 编码提升完全来自后训练,同一个底座,靠的是 slime 异步 RL 基础设施 ￼。也就是说,差距收窄的引擎是算法效率,而算法效率恰恰是开放研究里扩散最快的东西。你封不住论文,也封不住一个想法。

要回答你的问题,得先把”被超越”拆成四个不同的层,因为美国在每一层的处境完全不同:

一、前沿能力(谁先训出下一个最强的)。 美国仍领先,但这是跑步机不是护城河。原因有一个很脏但很关键的事实:GLM 系列在非常规探测下约 50% 的概率自称是 Claude,DeepSeek 也曾自称 ChatGPT ￼。这是蒸馏的指纹。它两头都割:一方面戳破”人家用零头算力就做到了”的神话——前沿那部分最贵的 R&D 是美国出钱探的;另一方面,它暴露了美国闭源商业模式的结构性漏桶——你花几十亿把前沿往前推,快速跟随者用一小笔钱蒸馏走九成。前沿在泄漏。这正是模型层注定商品化的微观机制。

二、单位算力/单位美元的能力(效率)。 这一层中国可能已经领先,而且是被逼出来的。这是你熟悉的霍尔木兹逻辑:卡点(chokepoint)不消灭对手,它招来绕行方案。出口管制没有冻结中国,它制造了 DeepSeek 的效率突破、slime、和昇腾的产业闭环。你越捏,对方的自给自足来得越快——管制在自我清算它本想守护的那个优势。

三、商业模式(这才是真正的不对称)。 中国在用 MIT 开源主动把模型层商品化。GLM-5.2 大约比 Claude / GPT-5 便宜十倍,MIT 许可,无地域限制,可自托管、可微调、可商用 ￼。如果模型是大宗商品,那美国在前沿的领先在商业上就不值钱了——除非那点能力差能撑得起十倍溢价。在大多数实际工作负载上撑不起。这是用开源把对手的利润池抽干的阳谋。

四、扩散与全球采用。 免费 + 便宜 + 无地域限制,赢的是全球南方和成本敏感型企业。美国闭源的溢价只在能力差足够大的高端场景成立。

那么美国真正相对耐久的优势在哪里?注意,几乎全都不在模型本身:

第一,算力供应链卡点——TSMC 先进制程、ASML、英伟达、CUDA。这是唯一真正的结构性筹码,但它正在被昇腾这件事侵蚀,而且双刃。这里有个值得你认真对待的反方观点:让中国依赖美国栈(英伟达、CUDA),可能比逼它自立更能拖长美国的领先。从这个角度,出口管制在战略上可能是适得其反的——它把一个偶然优势(谁正好控制了供应链)误当成可以靠封锁固化的永久优势。

第二,资本深度与宏观吸纳力。这大概是最耐久的一条,而它是个金融优势,不是技术优势。前沿训练以十亿美元计,微软/谷歌/亚马逊/Meta 加上美国 VC 能以中国国内无法匹配的规模持续投入——尤其在你那套资产负债表衰退框架下:通缩、去杠杆、企业资本开支疲软、地方财政吃紧。Zhipu IPO 募了约 5.58 亿美元、市值约 440 亿 ￼,真实,但相对于美国超大厂的投入是个零头。中国 AI 实验室在资本上被约束的程度,是美国实验室没有的。

第三,应用与集成层、企业分发与可信度。如果模型商品化,价值就上移到不商品化的层——这正是你 RCM 世界里的直觉:护城河在 workflow,不在 weights。Epic、合规信任、企业软件版图、API 生态——这一层美国结构性地强。

所以,回到你的提法”如何不被超越”,我的回答是:这个目标设定本身可能是错的。

如果”超越”指前沿能力——你只能靠砸更多算力、永远先推出下一个,来保持领先。但这是跑步机:因为泄漏(蒸馏)和效率扩散(开放研究),每一轮要花更多钱换更少的相对优势。你阻止不了被复制,只能跑得更快,而这越来越不划算。

如果”超越”指商业与经济主导——美国”赢”不靠拥有最聪明的模型,而靠在不商品化的层上攫取价值:供应链卡点(只要还守得住)、集成应用层、可信企业分发、以及为前沿融资和大规模部署的宏观能力。这条务实的路线,基本与跑分无关。

真正能让美国”输”的,从来不是一个更强的中国模型。是两件事:一,模型层商品化侵蚀掉那份供养前沿的经济回报;二,出口管制反噬,亲手替对手锻造出供应链独立性。GLM-5 跑在十万颗昇腾上、并在管制落地 48 小时后甩出 5.2,这两件事正在你眼前同时发生。

一句话:美国没有模型层面的”根本优势”,只有一个正在泄漏的领先和几条位于模型上下游、性质各异的真护城河。把战略目标定成”在 SWE-bench 上不被超越”,恰恰是看错了棋盘。

(顺带一个证伪自己的提醒:我对 GLM-5.2 的判断很大程度上建立在 Zhipu 自报和早期上手测试上——发布时官方没出基准,独立评测要再等两三周 ￼。蒸馏的 50% 自称 Claude 也提示,它的部分能力是”借”来的,真正自主探索前沿的成本还没由中国这边付过。这两点都该计入你对”差距”的折现里。)

author: rentierdigital
text:
fable 5 went offline in 12 hours. no deprecation window. no migration path. entire production pipeline dependent on 1 frontier model, and 1 government letter killed it globally.

the real move wasn't finding the next best model on the leaderboard. it was asking: what were we actually buying by routing everything through a single oracle?

turns out, something structurally better exists.

a panel of models with role diversity (security architect, skeptical economist, systems historian) plus a frontier judge synthesizing their disagreements scored 69.0% on DRACO deep research benchmarks. fable 5 solo scored 65.3%. the budget panel (gemini 3 flash, kimi k2.6, deepseek v4 pro) scored 64.7% at 40% of the cost.

the insight buried in those numbers: the architecture of deliberation outperforms the intelligence of any individual voice. management figured this out decades ago (committees, red teams, peer review). ai development spent 5 years chasing smarter single models without asking whether 3 medium-capable systems forced into structured disagreement might outperform 1 exceptional one uncontested.

turns out they might.

the perspective council stacks model diversity and role diversity at the same time. each panelist gets a different expert persona. the judge reads all responses, notes agreements and contradictions, synthesizes from the pattern. slower than a sprint. generally more right.

i build and ship daily. Claude Code, Codex, whatever ships fastest. SaaS, tools, automations. ⭐ if AI can build it, i've probably broken it first. what works → link in bio

author: zubiqo
text:
NEW: 🔬 OpenRouter Fuses Cheap Models to Mimic Fable 5

OpenRouter has launched Fusion, an API that runs prompts across multiple cheaper AI models simultaneously and synthesizes the outputs to rival expensive frontier models. The launch comes immediately after Anthropic suspended its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for foreign nationals worldwide due to a U.S. export control directive.

Fusion sends queries to a panel of parallel models equipped with web search and bash tools, using a judge model to extract consensus and a Claude Opus 4.8 synthesizer to compile the final answer.

On Perplexity’s DRACO deep research benchmark, a cheap mixture of Gemini 3 Flash, Kimi K2.6, and DeepSeek V4 Pro synthesized by Opus scored 64.7%.

This multi-model combination beat solo GPT-5.5 at 60% and solo Opus 4.8 at 58.8%, finishing within a point of solo Fable 5 at 65.3% for approximately half the cost.

OpenRouter acknowledged that Fusion cannot fully replace Fable 5, as it underperforms on long-horizon tasks and cannot act as a wholesale swap for complex coding.

"A way bigger deal than it seems." — Andrew Trask

Frontier labs lose their absolute moat when clever server-side orchestration achieves comparable reasoning benchmarks for a fraction of the price. However, needing to manually patch the system to stop web-searching models from scraping the evaluation rubric shows how fragile these synthetic stacks can be.

Source: Decrypt

Cybersecurity researchers immediately signed an open letter calling the move dangerous. Anthropic pointed out the same jailbreaks exist in other models.

The irony: the ban might actually be helping Anthropic. Sales data suggests the Trump admin feud is accidentally strengthening the brand. Streisand effect in AI regulation.

This follows the pattern we saw with encryption export controls in the 90s — restricting capability rarely stops proliferation, but it does signal which tools actually work.

https://t.co/dDrCxwEtTG

text:
security standards

The White House and Anthropic PBC are discussing new standards for evaluating security flaws in advanced artificial intelligence models, Politico reported on Thursday, citing administration officials.
Officials are seeking a common method for assessing vulnerabilities known as "jailbreaks," which allow users to bypass an AI model's safeguards. According to the report, the framework could help determine the severity of future incidents and when government intervention may be necessary.
The talks come as Anthropic seeks to lift restrictions on its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. The discussions follow a dispute over a security flaw in the company's latest AI systems that led Washington to impose export controls and restrict access for foreign users.

author: atmapshock
text:
US Government AI Model Export Controls and Cybersecurity Industry Operational Constraints: Policy Alignment Assessment

The US government's June 12 directive marked the first time Washington explicitly limited the release of a frontier AI model, and the industry response has exposed a structural fault line in how export control architecture applies to dual-use AI. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security directed Anthropic to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for any foreign national, whether inside or outside the United States, including Anthropic's own employees, forcing the company to disable both models for all customers to ensure compliance. A coordinated open letter from more than a hundred senior security practitioners argues the move harms defenders more than attackers. The interplay between export control objectives and operational security tooling needs is not marginal: the Mythos models were already demonstrating measurable defensive value, and their sudden withdrawal creates a capability gap that adversaries, unconstrained by the same directive, do not face.

author: cogan
text:
GLM 5.2 is absolutely a moment.

I’m using it as a coding agent through an API, not locally, and the results are remarkable. Frontier-level enough that I’d seriously consider it as the primary model behind an agent. And it costs far less than the closed frontier.

But Greg’s last line is the important one: "2027 is probably the year of local AI."

Because local frontier AI is not really here for most people today.

Yes, you can download the weights. Yes, you can run it yourself. But running a model this large well still requires an extraordinary amount of memory and accelerator hardware. The cost puts it outside the reach of almost everyone. Not to mention how difficult it is to even source the necessary hardware specs right now even if you have the capital to outlay.

That doesn’t diminish the moment. It defines it.

The model exists. The capability is here. The hardware just hasn’t caught up for the mass market yet.

But models are getting more efficient. Quantization is improving. Hardware will improve. Frontier-class intelligence will move onto machines ordinary people can actually own. That's why I appreciate Greg's directional 2027 caveat.

And after the Fable fiasco, the importance of that is impossible to miss.

We need open-weight models that cannot be switched off because a company, government, policy change, or geopolitical dispute says so.

We need intelligence we can possess, not merely rent.

GLM 5.2 is not that future for the average person yet.

But it makes that future feel considerably closer.

And I suspect that makes the closed frontier labs very nervous.

author: patrickojo_
text:
Last week the US government disabled Fable 5 and Mythos 5 overnight with no warning.

This week GLM-5.2 shows you can run a model matching that capability tier locally, on hardware you own, with no dependency on anyone’s export control directive, terms of service, or pricing decision.

The timing could not make the argument more clearly. Frontier-adjacent capability is no longer locked behind a small number of labs with kill-switch power. The companies building sovereign inference into their architecture right now are the ones who won’t be disrupted next time this happens, and there will be a next time.
